payload.claim: If the SDK-path probe on the previous line (`_sdk=$(... import claude_agent_sdk ...)`) produces no output (import fails, e.g. `__file__` unset or the interpreter errors, with stderr discarded), `_sdk` is the empty string. `dirname ""` in GNU coreutils returns `.`, which always exists as the shell's cwd, so this line silently probes the current working directory instead of the SDK's site-packages parent and always emits `wrote .` or `refused .` rather than `missing`. This defeats the self-check's stated purpose of catching a misbuilt image: a genuinely broken SDK path can still contribute a `refused` line (from an unrelated directory) toward the six-refusal threshold instead of surfacing as a `missing` line, and no test in this diff exercises the case where the SDK-path lookup itself fails.
